raw_case_text: We present the case of an 18-month-old female patient with PB following pneumonia. At 2 months of age, the patient was hospitalized due to pneumonia. At 6 months of age, she underwent a palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure (Fontan-type) due to CHD (double-inlet and double-outlet ventricle with common atrioventricular canal). The perioperative period was uneventful. Echocardiography at 12 and 18 months of age showed proper heart function (ejection fraction, 67%). At 18 months of age, she was again hospitalized due to pneumonia that remained unresolved after three courses of antibiotics in the home setting. Infiltration and atelectasis of the left upper lobe had been clinically suspected (because of dullness and diminished breath sounds over that region) and was confirmed by a chest X-ray. Blood pressure was normal. However, SpO2 was approximately 50% (having previously been at 70-80%). In addition, hypogammaglobulinemia was detected. In the differential diagnosis, we excluded atopy, cystic fibrosis, immunodeficiency disorders, viral infections (with cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and pneumotropic viruses), and fungal infections (Aspergillus sp. and Candida sp.). Within a few days, her coughs were more productive and there was expectoration of small mucoid casts. Despite antibiotic treatment, gamma-globulin replacement therapy, oxygen therapy, and intensive chest physiotherapy, as well as the use of nebulized bronchodilators and mucolytics, there was no clinical improvement. On post-admission day 17, fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FB) revealed complete obliteration of the left bronchus. Application of suction allowed to remove bronchial casts, followed by bronchial lavage of that region (Figure 1). Cultures of the bronchial lavage fluid were negative for fungi and bacteria. Microscopic analysis of the material collected revealed type-1 bronchial casts. After the bronchoscopy, the inflammation of the left lobes was resolved. Treatment with azithromycin, systemic and inhaled steroids, () and enalapril maleate was initiated, as was the use of nebulized 3% NaCl solution plus a bronchodilator. One week after treatment initiation, a control FB revealed only small fragments of casts, which were removed easily and completely. On post-admission day 33, the patient was discharged.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 18-month-old female with complex congenital heart disease status post bidirectional Glenn procedure presented with persistent pneumonia, severe hypoxemia, and productive cough with expectoration of small mucoid bronchial casts.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Having undergone a palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure at 6 months of age, the patient was hospitalized at 18 months of age for pneumonia that failed to resolve after three outpatient antibiotic courses. Within a few days of admission, her cough became increasingly productive with expectoration of small mucoid casts and severe hypoxemia (SpO2 dropping from a baseline of 70%-80% to ~50%), refractory to IV antibiotics, IVIG, oxygen, chest physiotherapy, and nebulized bronchodilators/mucolytics.
subjective.past_medical_history: Complex congenital heart disease (double-inlet and double-outlet ventricle with common atrioventricular canal) status post palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure at 6 months of age; prior hospitalization for pneumonia at 2 months of age.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent productive cough, expectoration of mucoid bronchial casts, and severe cyanosis/hypoxemia.

objective.physical_examination: Normal blood pressure, severe hypoxemia with SpO2 ~50% (baseline 70%-80%), and dullness to percussion with diminished breath sounds over the left upper lung zone.
objective.routine_investigations: Echocardiography at 12 and 18 months showed preserved ventricular systolic function (LVEF 67%). Chest X-ray confirmed left upper lobe infiltration and atelectasis. Laboratory workup revealed hypogammaglobulinemia, while testing for atopy, cystic fibrosis, primary immunodeficiency, viral infections (CMV, EBV, pneumotropic viruses), and fungal infections (Aspergillus spp. and Candida spp.) was negative.
objective.advanced_workup: On hospital day 17, fiberoptic bronchoscopy revealed complete obliteration of the left main bronchus by branching bronchial casts, which were removed by bronchoscopic suctioning and lavage; repeat bronchoscopy 1 week later cleared small residual cast fragments. Bronchial lavage fluid bacterial and fungal cultures were negative, and histopathology of the extracted casts confirmed acellular/inflammatory type-1 fibrinous/mucoid bronchial casts.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Plastic bronchitis (type-1 bronchial casts) complicating palliative bidirectional Glenn circulation and pneumonia in an 18-month-old child; allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis and invasive fungal infections (Aspergillus spp. and Candida spp.) were excluded by negative mycological workup and negative bronchial lavage cultures. Successfully treated with bronchoscopic suction extraction of the obstructing left bronchial casts (days 17 and 24), azithromycin, systemic and inhaled corticosteroids, sildenafil, enalapril maleate, and nebulized 3% hypertonic saline with bronchodilators, resulting in resolution of left lung atelectasis and hospital discharge on day 33.
